hero.lead: A principality of 41,000 in the Alps, which joined the IMF in October 2024 as its 191st member, with public debt of 0.5% of GDP.

capital.heading: A principality that owes almost nothing.

register.name: Housing for people in need of protection, Unterland
register.detail: Finanzbeschluss of the Landtag of 5 December 2024 · LGBl. 2025 Nr. 64, 24 January 2025 · commitment credit CHF 1.2 million · supplementary credits of CHF 1.405 million for 2025 · up to 70 people in Eschen
register.note: A vacant commercial building in the Eschen industrial area converted into collective housing; the Government’s timetable set opening for November 2025
register.text: A commitment credit approved by the Landtag to convert a vacant commercial building in Eschen into collective housing for up to 70 people in need of protection, with supplementary credits in the 2025 budget for its first equipment, rent and running costs. It finances a roof for people the state has taken under its protection, which serves the shelter standard.
by: Landtag of the Principality of Liechtenstein
Government of the Principality of Liechtenstein

register.name: IMF membership quota
register.detail: International Monetary Fund · member since 21 October 2024, the 191st · initial quota SDR 100 million, about US$134.7 million · Article IV consultations concluded March 2025 and March 2026
register.note: The quota determines Liechtenstein’s capital subscription to the Fund; the 2026 consultation found a fiscal surplus of 2.8% of GDP in 2025
register.text: Liechtenstein’s initial quota at the International Monetary Fund, which it joined on 21 October 2024 as the 191st member; a member’s quota determines its capital subscription. Membership brings the IMF’s Article IV review of the economy and of the public finances that pay for the seven standards, concluded in March 2025 and again in March 2026.
by: Government of the Principality of Liechtenstein

register.name: Inaugural Liechtenstein Pfandbriefe
register.detail: Liechtensteinisches Pfandbriefinstitut · announced 1 April 2026 · two tranches, 5 and 10 years · yields to maturity 0.593% and 0.875% · rated Aaa by Moody’s · listed on SIX Swiss Exchange from 22 April 2026
register.note: The first covered bonds of the institute, under the Pfandbriefe act adopted by the Landtag in December 2024
register.text: The first issue of the Liechtensteinisches Pfandbriefinstitut, founded in January 2026 by LGT and Liechtensteinische Landesbank as a shared platform for Liechtenstein banks to issue covered bonds. The bonds are secured by first-lien mortgages on Liechtenstein real estate and broaden the banks’ refinancing base for home loans, which bears on the shelter standard.

items.label: Land area, 2023

items.name: The Income
items.label: GDP a person, 2024
items.text: Output a person on a scale that can finance far beyond the nation’s own borders.

items.name: Solargenossenschaft Liechtenstein
items.text: A cooperative founded in 1992 that builds and runs solar plants on public and company roofs and sells their power; it lists ten plants in operation, six of them commissioned between November 2024 and February 2025, and sells the electricity of its new plants on Triesen’s municipal buildings to the municipality for 20 years at favourable tariffs.

items.name: Familienhilfe Liechtenstein
items.text: An independent foundation under public law since January 2024 that provides home nursing (Spitex), household support and a meal service, billed by the hour; in 2025 its 260 staff served 1,668 clients with 212,864 billable hours and delivered 29,769 meals to 285 people.

items.name: Heilpädagogisches Zentrum (hpz)
items.text: A foundation in Schaan whose workshops give supported work to people with disabilities in six departments that sell products and services; at the end of 2025 some 220 supported workers worked there, and its production earned CHF 1.18 million in the year.
